newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia fund approves first export credits - papers.
newsitem.headline: Serbia fund approves first export credits - papers.

text.p: The Serbian government has approved the first 45 credits worth 126 million German marks ($71.9 million) from Serbia's Development Fund for stimulating exports and export-oriented production, Belgrade papers reported on Friday.

Individual loans are worth between 250,000 and 10 million German marks with four- to six-month repayment periods, depending on the production cycle, and four-percent interest per year, Belgrade daily Politika said.
In June, the Serbian government adopted a programme to finance exports aimed at helping cash-strapped industry revive production and double exports this year.
"There is no better reform than the one which begins with the rehabilitation of production capacities," Serbia's Privatisation Minister Milan Beko was quoted as saying.
The programme will also raise employment and ensure higher revenues for the state, which will ease public expenditure servicing, Beko said.
The credits, granted only for export deals already concluded, are repayable in hard currency.
The government expects the loans to the 45 firms will secure exports worth 656 million marks.
It said the contracted export deals would raise average use of capacities in those firms from 55 to 80 percent and reactivate some 12,000 workers.

The Serbian Development Fund is the sole recipient of 1.568 billion German marks raised through the sale of a 49-percent stake in Serbia's telecom company Telekom Srbija to OTE of Greece and Stet of Italy, 80 percent of which was paid immediately. The rest will be paid in January.

The credit deals were signed with firms from all of Serbia and from various branches of industry, including textile, leather and footwear, chemicals, electrical appliances, wood-processing, shipbuilding, metal processing and mining.

Recipients of the maximum credits of 10 million marks include furniture and household fixtures factory Simpo of Vranje, Yumco clothing manufacturer of Vranje and HIP petrohemija chemicals industry of Pancevo.

Krusevac engine factory 14 oktobar received a loan of seven million, ferro-nickel producer Feronikl of Glogovac six million, Gosa Holding Corporation mining equipment producer of Smederevska Palanka five million and Sava shipyard of Sremska Mitrovica 3.5 million marks. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305 ($ = 1.753 German Marks)
